metas.name: Amazon
metas.note:
The Amazon area is very distinct. It is fairly flat, and contains many of these trees with white bark (Cordia trichotoma), and oil palms.

The vast majority of the coverage notably uses the rarer “high antenna”.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Banana Plants
metas.note: Banana plants, and especially plantations, are most commonly found in the southwestern part of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: E40 Salinas-Guayaquil
metas.note: The E-40 between Salinas and Guayaquil is one of the only divided highways in Ecuador, and the only one in the dry area near the southwestern coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Esmeraldas Province
metas.note: The province of Esmeraldas can look similar to the Amazon region, but it is significantly hillier.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Extremly Dry
metas.note: This extremely dry landscape is only found in the coastal region between Guayaquil and Manta.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Galapagos Islands
metas.note: The Galapagos Islands are an archipelago located west of mainland Ecuador. There are only trekkers and boat coverage on and around the islands. There is a wide variety of landscapes, including volcanic soil, low shrubbery, and craters (with Galapagos turtles onlooking).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Gen 4 Appearance
metas.note:
Generation 4 cannot be found in the north-west and in the south-east.

NOTE: If the cabel (second image & not always visible) goes to the center of the car, you are in Quito.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: High/Low Antenna
metas.note:
The Google car antenna has two distinct variations:

The “high” antenna (purple), where the wire around the antenna is entirely above the halfway line of the antenna.

And the “low” antenna (blue) where the majority of the wire is below the halfway point of the line, and there can be a small bit poking up at the very top.

This is most useful when you have the high antenna, since it will always be in the northern half of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Loja Pole
metas.note: Electricity poles with oval, see-through holes are most common in Loja province. They are occasionally found in neighbouring provinces.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Semi-Arid Chimborazo
metas.note: The province of Chimborazo is semi-arid, and has an abundance of pine trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Southern Provinces
metas.note:
The southern regions have many winding mountain roads and exposed brownish red dirt.

The central provinces can have similar roads, but the exposed dirt will usually not be found in these areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Street Signs
metas.note: Street are sometimes unique to a specific city. See the graphic for the most important ones.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Taxis Letters
metas.note:
Taxis in Ecuador are very common, and the first letter on each taxi can be used to determine the province you are in. The first letter of the taxi and the first letter of the province name are often the same.

NOTE: This letter will also appear as the first letter on ordinary licence plates respectively in each region. Beware that the letter P, as the letter for Pichincha (the region containing Quito), shows up occasionally in several regions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Yellow/Black-Guardrail
metas.note: Guardrails in Guayas province are often painted black-and-yellow, as opposed to the generic silver or solid yellow versions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.
